## 1. GLOBAL MACRO OVERVIEW

The inflation and policy picture has evolved meaningfully since yesterday. Wednesday's June PPI data confirmed a -1.26% month-on-month decline (as of June, per FRED) — the largest drop in 14 months, driven by falling energy costs — following Tuesday's CPI surprise [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/PPIACO; https://www.reuters.com/business/us-producer-prices-unexpectedly-fall-june-2026-07-15/]. With both CPI at 3.73% YoY (down from 4.27% in May) and PPI falling sharply, economists now estimate core PCE inflation rose only 0.2% in June (translating to approximately 3.3% YoY), providing the Fed with significant breathing room [Source: https://www.reuters.com/business/us-producer-prices-unexpectedly-fall-june-2026-07-15/]. Fed Chair Warsh's congressional testimony Wednesday reinforced this nuance: inflation "slowed sharply in June" and the Fed has "no tolerance" for persistently elevated inflation, but stopped short of a hawkish commitment — markets dialled back July hike probabilities to 17% on his testimony combined with the CPI data [Source: https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/14/business/live-news/cpi-inflation-kevin-warsh-capitol-hill-testimony]. The 10-year Treasury yield stands at 4.58% and the 2-year at 4.18% as of July 14 [Source: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10; https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS2] — marginally lower than yesterday's 4.62%/4.26%, consistent with the disinflation repricing.

However, the BOK shock this morning is the dominant new development for Thursday's session. The Bank of Korea raised its benchmark rate by 25bp to 2.75% — the first hike since January 2023 — citing consumer price inflation above 3% in both May and June, driven by energy costs from the US-Iran conflict and won weakness [Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/16/bok-interest-rate-monetary-policy-markets-kospi-skhynix.html]. Economists polled by Reuters had expected the move, but markets clearly did not fully price it: KOSPI collapsed -6.37% to 6,820.60, erasing essentially all of yesterday's +6.3% recovery in a single session [Source: Yahoo Finance (^KS11)]. The BOK statement explicitly noted inflation is likely to remain above the 2% target "for a considerable time" and that further tightening is likely — a hawkish forward guidance that mirrors the Waller/Warsh posture in the US [Source: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/16/bok-interest-rate-monetary-policy-markets-kospi-skhynix.html]. This signals that the Iran-energy-inflation transmission is forcing global tightening, even as US disinflation data provides temporary relief.

US equities extended their recovery in Wednesday's session, with the S&P 500 reaching 7,572.40 (+0.38%), the Dow 52,658.64 (+0.29%), while the Nasdaq 100 dipped -0.28% to 29,502.60 amid continued semiconductor sector weakness [Source: Yahoo Finance (^GSPC); Yahoo Finance (^DJI); Yahoo Finance (^NDX)]. VIX is mildly elevated at 15.84 (+1.08%) — still below 16, but ticking higher this morning as Asian risk-off spreads [Source: Yahoo Finance (^VIX)]. The earnings season context remains constructive: Morgan Stanley, BlackRock, and Johnson & Johnson all reported before Wednesday's bell, while United Airlines reported after the close — with the broad earnings backdrop characterised as "cooling rate fears, strong earnings" [Source: https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/us-futures-rise-on-cooling-rate-fears-strong-earnings-iran-strikes-continue-4792073]. However, ASML's strong earnings (a bullish AI demand signal) were unable to prevent the Nasdaq 100 from slipping, as chip stocks sold off despite the positive equipment maker print [Source: https://ca.finance.yahoo.com/news/stock-market-today-wednesday-july-15-dow-sp-nasdaq-091813320.html].

Oil remains the structural wildcard. Brent crude at $84.48 (-0.55%) and WTI at $79.41 (-0.24%) are modestly lower today — a marginal pullback from the $85-86 range that has prevailed for three sessions — but the Strait of Hormuz situation has not meaningfully de-escalated [Source: Yahoo Finance (BZ=F); Yahoo Finance (CL=F)]. ### Disputed

- [CPI at 3.73% YoY]: The FRED bundle data shows CPI YoY at 3.73% as_of 2026-06-01, but the Reuters CPI article clearly states the June CPI annual rate is 3.5% YoY. The report uses 3.73% in the macro data section but correctly references 3.5% in narrative text. The FRED figure (3.73%) appears to be an older or differently-dated reading; the current June CPI YoY per news sources is 3.5%, not 3.73%. This discrepancy is internal to the bundle itself but the report's use of "3.73% YoY" in the overview section without flagging the June print of 3.5% is potentially misleading.

- [Report states 10Y yield moved "marginally lower than yesterday's 4.62%/4.26%"]: The bundle shows 10Y at 4.58% and 2Y at 4.18% as_of 2026-07-14 — these are the most recent available figures. There is no today's (July 16) Treasury data in the bundle to confirm the directional claim of "marginally lower." The prior session values of 4.62%/4.26% referenced are not in the bundle and cannot be verified, though per the continuity context rule this is not disputed solely on that basis. However, the directional claim of yields moving lower is consistent with the disinflation narrative.

- [Report claims silver was at "yesterday's $58.655"]: The bundle shows silver at $57.21 (+0.18%) as_of 2026-07-16. If yesterday's close was $58.655 and today is $57.21, that would represent a -2.46% decline, not the +0.18% change shown in the bundle. The +0.18% change_pct in the data conflicts with the implied prior-day level of $58.655 cited in the report. Either the prior-day value is incorrect, or the change_pct in the bundle reflects a different reference period.

- [Report references "46.5% chance of July Fed rate hike" on Monday per CME FedWatch]: The CNBC article confirms this figure as of Monday July 13 (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/13/-a-july-rate-hike-from-the-fed-the-odds-are-rising.html). The report's Executive Summary states the probability was "42%" two days ago, not 46.5%. Both figures come from the news bundle (CNN article states 42% "one day ago" from Tuesday's perspective; CNBC states 46.5% on Monday). The exact peak probability is 46.5% (Monday), not 42% as stated in the Executive Summary. Minor but factually imprecise.

- [BTC at "yesterday's $64,595"]: The bundle does not contain a prior-day BTC value to verify this figure. Not disputed under the continuity rule, but flagged as unverifiable.
